## About the bill

This bill became the vehicle for passage of the FIRST Step Act, the Senate’s criminal justice reform bill. The text of this bill was replaced in whole on December 18, 2018 with criminal justice reform provisions. Those provisions were originally introduced in [S. 2795](https://www.govtrack.us/congress/bills/115/s2795) and [H.R. 5682](https://www.govtrack.us/congress/bills/115/hr5682).

Prior to becoming the vehicle for passage of criminal justice reform, this bill was the Save Our Seas Act of 2018.

### S. 756 (115th) was a bill in the United States Congress.

A bill must be passed by both the House and Senate in identical form and then be signed by the President to become law.

Bills numbers restart every two years. That means there are other bills with the number S. 756. This is the one from the 115 th Congress.

This bill was introduced in the 115 th Congress, which met from Jan. 3, 2017 to Jan. 3, 2019. Legislation not passed by the end of a Congress is cleared from the books.

## About the bill

This bill became the vehicle for passage of the FIRST Step Act, the Senate’s criminal justice reform bill. The text of this bill was replaced in whole on December 18, 2018 with criminal justice reform provisions. Those provisions were originally introduced in [S. 2795](https://www.govtrack.us/congress/bills/115/s2795) and [H.R. 5682](https://www.govtrack.us/congress/bills/115/hr5682).

Prior to becoming the vehicle for passage of criminal justice reform, this bill was the Save Our Seas Act of 2018.

# Sen. Robert “Rob” Portman

Former Senator for Ohio

pronounced RAH-bert // PORT-min

Portman was a senator from [Ohio](https://www.govtrack.us/congress/members/OH) and was a Republican. He served from 2011 to 2022.

He was previously the representative for [Ohio](https://www.govtrack.us/congress/members/OH)’s 2 nd congressional district as a Republican from May 4, 1993 to April 29, 2005.

# Sen. Robert “Rob” Portman

Former Senator for Ohio

pronounced RAH-bert // PORT-min

Portman was a senator from [Ohio](https://www.govtrack.us/congress/members/OH) and was a Republican. He served from 2011 to 2022.

He was previously the representative for [Ohio](https://www.govtrack.us/congress/members/OH)’s 2 nd congressional district as a Republican from May 4, 1993 to April 29, 2005.

**Cynthia Jeanne Shaheen** ([/ˈ dʒ iː n ʃ ə ˈ h iː n/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_JEEN shə-HEEN_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); née **Bowers**, born January 28, 1947) is an American politician and former educator serving since 2009 as the [senior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seniority_in_the_United_States_Senate "Seniority in the United States Senate")[United States senator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") from [New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire "New Hampshire"). A member of the [Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)"), she served from 1997 to 2003 as the [78th governor of New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_Hampshire "List of governors of New Hampshire"). Shaheen is the first woman elected both [governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_(United_States) "Governor (United States)") and a U.S. senator, and was the first elected [female governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States "List of female governors in the United States") of New Hampshire.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-1)

After serving two terms in the [New Hampshire Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire_Senate "New Hampshire Senate"), Shaheen was elected governor in [1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_New_Hampshire_gubernatorial_election "1996 New Hampshire gubernatorial election") and reelected in [1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_New_Hampshire_gubernatorial_election "1998 New Hampshire gubernatorial election") and [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_New_Hampshire_gubernatorial_election "2000 New Hampshire gubernatorial election"). In [2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "2002 United States Senate election in New Hampshire"), she unsuccessfully ran for the U.S. Senate against [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") nominee [John E. Sununu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_E._Sununu "John E. Sununu"). She served as director of the [Harvard Institute of Politics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Institute_of_Politics "Harvard Institute of Politics") before resigning to run for the U.S. Senate again in the [2008 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "2008 United States Senate election in New Hampshire"), defeating Sununu in a rematch. She has been the dean of [New Hampshire’s congressional delegation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire's_congressional_delegations "New Hampshire's congressional delegations") since 2011, when Senator [Judd Gregg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judd_Gregg "Judd Gregg") retired.

Shaheen became the first Democratic senator from New Hampshire since [John A. Durkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_A._Durkin "John A. Durkin"). In [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "2014 United States Senate election in New Hampshire"), she became the second Democrat from New Hampshire to be reelected to the Senate since [Thomas J. McIntyre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_J._McIntyre "Thomas J. McIntyre") in [1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "1972 United States Senate election in New Hampshire"). She was reelected to a third term in [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "2020 United States Senate election in New Hampshire"). Upon [Dianne Feinstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dianne_Feinstein "Dianne Feinstein")'s death in 2023, Shaheen became the oldest serving female U.S. senator. On March 12, 2025, she announced that she would not seek reelection in [2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "2026 United States Senate election in New Hampshire").

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Jeanne Shaheen was born Cynthia Jeanne Bowers in [St. Charles, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri "St. Charles, Missouri"), the daughter of Belle Ernestine (Stillings) and Ivan E. Bowers.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-2)[_[unreliable source?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable\_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")_]

Shaheen graduated from high school in [Selinsgrove, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selinsgrove,_Pennsylvania "Selinsgrove, Pennsylvania"), and earned a bachelor's degree in English from [Shippensburg University of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shippensburg_University_of_Pennsylvania "Shippensburg University of Pennsylvania") and a master's degree in political science from the [University of Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Mississippi "University of Mississippi").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-10things-3) She taught high school in [Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi "Mississippi")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-4) and moved to New Hampshire in 1973, where she also taught school.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-5)

## Early political career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early political career")]

As a [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Democratic_Party "United States Democratic Party"), she worked on several campaigns, including [Jimmy Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter "Jimmy Carter")'s 1976 presidential campaign, and as the New Hampshire campaign manager for [Gary Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Hart "Gary Hart") in 1984,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-6) before running for office in 1990, when she was elected to the [state Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire_Senate "New Hampshire Senate") for the [21st district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire's_21st_State_Senate_District "New Hampshire's 21st State Senate District"). She was elected [governor of New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_New_Hampshire "Governor of New Hampshire") in 1996 and reelected in 1998 and 2000.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-7)

In April 2005, Shaheen was named director of Harvard's Institute of Politics,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-8) succeeding former U.S. Representative and Secretary of Agriculture [Dan Glickman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Glickman "Dan Glickman").

## Governorship

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Governorship")]

Shaheen's decision to run for New Hampshire governor followed the retirement of Republican Governor [Steve Merrill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Merrill "Steve Merrill"). Her opponent in 1996 was [Ovide M. Lamontagne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovide_M._Lamontagne "Ovide M. Lamontagne"), then chairman of the State Board of Education. Shaheen presented herself as a moderate. According to a PBS profile, she focused on education funding issues, and pledged to expand kindergarten. She defeated Lamontagne by 87,854 votes.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-9)

Shaheen was the first woman to be elected governor of New Hampshire.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-10) (She was not, however, the first woman to serve as New Hampshire's governor; [Vesta M. Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vesta_M._Roy "Vesta M. Roy") was acting governor from December 30, 1982, until January 6, 1983.)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-11)

In 1998, she was reelected by 112,296 votes.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-13)

In both 1996 and 1998, Shaheen took a no-new-taxes pledge. After a court decision preventing education from being largely supported by local taxes, "her administration devised a plan that would have increased education spending and set a statewide property tax."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-14)

Running for a third term in 2000, Shaheen refused to renew her no-new-taxes pledge, becoming the first New Hampshire governor in 38 years to win an election without making that pledge.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-15) Shaheen's preferred solution to the school-funding problem was not a broad-based tax but legalized video-gambling at state racetracks—a solution repeatedly rejected by the state legislature.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-17)

In 2001, Shaheen tried to implement a 2.5% sales tax, the first broad-based tariff of its kind in New Hampshire, which has never had a sales tax. The state legislature rejected her proposal.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-18) She also proposed an increase in the state's cigarette tax and a 4.5% capital gains tax.

## Presidential politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Presidential politics")]

### 2000

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2000")]

During the [2000 Democratic presidential primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States)_presidential_primaries,_2000 "Democratic Party (United States) presidential primaries, 2000") in New Hampshire, Shaheen supported [Al Gore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore "Al Gore"), and her husband served as Gore's New Hampshire campaign manager. According to the _New York Observer_, the Shaheens were critical in helping Gore win a narrow victory in the New Hampshire primary over [Bill Bradley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Bradley "Bill Bradley").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-20)

Gore added Shaheen to his short list of potential vice presidential nominees, which also included Indiana Senator [Evan Bayh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Bayh "Evan Bayh"), North Carolina Senator [John Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Edwards "John Edwards"), House Minority Leader [Dick Gephardt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Gephardt "Dick Gephardt"), Massachusetts Senator [John Kerry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry "John Kerry"), and Connecticut Senator [Joe Lieberman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Lieberman "Joe Lieberman").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-21) Shaheen responded to speculation by stating she wasn't interested in the job.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-22) There has since been discussion over whether Gore would have won the election had he picked Shaheen as his running mate.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-24)

### 2004

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2004")]

After a short time teaching at [Harvard University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University") (and a fellowship in the Institute of Politics with former Massachusetts Governor [Jane Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane_Swift "Jane Swift")), Shaheen was named national chairperson of [John Kerry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry "John Kerry")'s [2004 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry_presidential_campaign,_2004 "John Kerry presidential campaign, 2004") in September 2003.

#### 2002

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2002")]

Main article: [2002 United States Senate election in New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "2002 United States Senate election in New Hampshire")

After three two-year terms as governor, Shaheen declined to run for a fourth, instead choosing to run for the U.S. Senate in [2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Senate_election,_2002 "U.S. Senate election, 2002"). Republican [John E. Sununu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_E._Sununu "John E. Sununu") defeated her by 19,751 votes. In an interview with the _[Concord Monitor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concord\_Monitor "Concord Monitor")_, Shaheen attributed her loss in part to "discussion about the job that [she] did as governor." At that time, early Republican advertisements slammed her support for putting a sales tax on the ballot or faulted her for failing schools.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-25)

In June 2004, former Republican consultant [Allen Raymond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Raymond "Allen Raymond") pleaded guilty to [jamming the phone lines of the New Hampshire Democratic Party's 2002 get-out-the-vote operation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_New_Hampshire_Senate_election_phone_jamming_scandal "2002 New Hampshire Senate election phone jamming scandal"); some believe this interference contributed to Shaheen's loss, including former Senator [Bob Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_C._Smith "Robert C. Smith"), whom Sununu had defeated in the Republican primary.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-26) In February 2005, a judge sentenced Raymond to five months in prison. Former state GOP executive director [Charles McGee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_McGee_(politician) "Charles McGee (politician)") was sentenced to seven months for his role.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-28)

Raymond alleged that [James Tobin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Tobin_(political_operative) "James Tobin (political operative)"), [Northeast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northeastern_United_States "Northeastern United States") field director for the [National Republican Senatorial Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Republican_Senatorial_Committee "National Republican Senatorial Committee"), masterminded the plot. In December 2005, Tobin was convicted of two federal felonies arising from the phone-jamming and sentenced to ten months in prison, but his conviction was reversed on appeal. In October 2008, prosecutors filed two new felony indictments charging that Tobin lied to an FBI agent when he was interviewed in 2003 about his role in the phone-jamming case.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-29) These charges were summarily dismissed in 2009 after the federal judge in Maine's District Court found them motivated by "vindictive prosecution".[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-Harrison-30)

#### 2008

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2008")]

Main article: [2008 United States Senate election in New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "2008 United States Senate election in New Hampshire")

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/Jeanne_Shaheen%2C_official_Senate_photo_portrait%2C_2009.jpg/250px-Jeanne_Shaheen%2C_official_Senate_photo_portrait%2C_2009.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jeanne_Shaheen,_official_Senate_photo_portrait,_2009.jpg)

Official portrait, 2009

In early July 2007, University of New Hampshire Survey Center poll found that even though Shaheen had not yet announced whether she would run for Senate, she would beat Sununu in the 2008 Senate race 54–38. By contrast, all the Democratic candidates already in the race trailed Sununu in polling.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-31)

In April 2007, Shaheen met with Senate Majority Leader [Harry Reid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Reid "Harry Reid") and [Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Senatorial_Campaign_Committee "Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee") Chairman [Chuck Schumer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Schumer "Chuck Schumer") about a Senate run. Both said she would have strong support from the DSCC if she ran. On September 14, 2007, Shaheen announced her candidacy.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-32) On September 15, she formally launched her campaign at her home in [Madbury, New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madbury,_New_Hampshire "Madbury, New Hampshire"). On September 21, [EMILY's List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMILY's_List "EMILY's List") endorsed her campaign.

Shaheen defeated Sununu by 44,535 votes.

Shaheen ran for reelection in 2014, facing former Massachusetts Senator [Scott Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Brown_(politician) "Scott Brown (politician)").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-33)

In March 2014, Brown announced he was forming an exploratory committee to run against Shaheen. According to the [Boston Herald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Herald "Boston Herald"), "Granite State Republicans are calling U.S. Sen. Jeanne Shaheen a hypocrite for asking potential GOP challenger and former U.S. Sen. Scott Brown to keep "outside" money out of the campaign while she fills the Democratic war chest on the West Coast".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-34)

In June 2014, WMUR reported that Shaheen had never released her tax returns in her 18 years of public service in New Hampshire. Shaheen said she would not rule out releasing her returns, but would like to see her opponent do so first.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-35)

She was endorsed again by Emily's List.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-36)

On election night, even as her party lost control of the Senate, Shaheen won reelection by 15,837 votes. As a measure of how Republican New Hampshire once was, Shaheen is only the second Democrat in the state's history to win two terms in the Senate.

#### 2020

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2020")]

Main article: [2020 United States Senate election in New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "2020 United States Senate election in New Hampshire")

Shaheen was reelected in 2020 defeating Republican nominee Bryant "Corky" Messner by 124,549 votes. She is the first New Hampshire Democrat elected to three full terms in the Senate. The only other Democrat to be popularly elected more than once from New Hampshire, [Thomas J. McIntyre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_J._McIntyre "Thomas J. McIntyre") (who held the seat Shaheen currently holds), served the remainder of [Styles Bridges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Styles_Bridges "Styles Bridges")'s last term before being elected to two terms in his own right.

On January 3, 2009, Shaheen was sworn in to the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate"). As a senator, she has sponsored 288 bills, five of which have become law.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-37)

On January 6, 2021, Shaheen was participating in the certification of the [2021 United States Electoral College vote count](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_United_States_Electoral_College_vote_count "2021 United States Electoral College vote count") when Trump supporters [attacked the U.S. Capitol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_6_United_States_Capitol_attack "January 6 United States Capitol attack"). She tweeted during the attack that she and her staff were safe and that "We will not be stopped from doing our Constitutional duty".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-West-38) The day after the attack, Shaheen called Trump "unfit for office" and said that she supported impeaching him and removing him from office.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-Brewer-39)

In 2024, Shaheen was ranked among the top 10 most bipartisan senators.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-40)

## Political positions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Political positions")]

### Healthcare

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Healthcare")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Healthcare_Presser_Gallery_073119_%2899_of_117%29_%2848424636752%29.jpg/250px-Healthcare_Presser_Gallery_073119_%2899_of_117%29_%2848424636752%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Healthcare_Presser_Gallery_073119_(99_of_117)_(48424636752).jpg)

Shaheen speaks on health care, 2019

In 2009, Shaheen partnered with U.S. Senator [Susan Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Collins_(politician) "Susan Collins (politician)") to introduce the Medicare Transitional Care Act, which provides follow-up care for discharged hospital patients to reduce re-hospitalizations.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-45) The bill passed in 2010,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-46) and research at the [University of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania "University of Pennsylvania") predicted the measure would lower the cost of healthcare by as much as $5,000 per Medicare beneficiary while also improving healthcare quality and reducing re-hospitalizations.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-47)

In December 2009, Shaheen voted for the [Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affordable_Care_Act "Affordable Care Act") (Obamacare).[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-49)

Before the rollout of the ACA, Shaheen said that people who liked their current healthcare plans could keep them.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-50) When asked about people who were losing their healthcare plans due to the ACA, Shaheen said they could keep their plans if they were "willing to pay more".[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-51)

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/U.S._Senator_Jeanne_Shaheen%2C_U.S._Congressman_Joe_Wilson%2C_U.S._envoy_to_Syria_Tom_Barrack%2C_and_Syrian_President_Ahmed_al-Sharaa_%282025%29.jpg/250px-U.S._Senator_Jeanne_Shaheen%2C_U.S._Congressman_Joe_Wilson%2C_U.S._envoy_to_Syria_Tom_Barrack%2C_and_Syrian_President_Ahmed_al-Sharaa_%282025%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:U.S._Senator_Jeanne_Shaheen,_U.S._Congressman_Joe_Wilson,_U.S._envoy_to_Syria_Tom_Barrack,_and_Syrian_President_Ahmed_al-Sharaa_(2025).jpg)

Shaheen, U.S. Congressman [Joe Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Wilson "Joe Wilson"), and U.S. envoy to Syria [Tom Barrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Barrack "Tom Barrack") met with Syrian President [Ahmed al-Sharaa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_al-Sharaa "Ahmed al-Sharaa"), August 2025

In August 2019, Shaheen was one of 19 senators to sign a letter to [Treasury Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_the_Treasury "United States Secretary of the Treasury")[Steven Mnuchin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Mnuchin "Steven Mnuchin") and [Health and Human Services Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Health_and_Human_Services "United States Secretary of Health and Human Services")[Alex Azar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Azar "Alex Azar") requesting data from the Trump administration to help states and Congress understand the potential consequences of the _Texas v. United States Affordable Care Act_ lawsuit, writing that an overhaul of the present health care system would form "an enormous hole in the pocketbooks of the people we serve as well as wreck state budgets".[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-52)

In October 2019, Shaheen was one of 27 senators to sign a letter to Senate Majority Leader [Mitch McConnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitch_McConnell "Mitch McConnell") and Senate Minority Leader [Chuck Schumer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Schumer "Chuck Schumer") advocating the passage of the Community Health Investment, Modernization, and Excellence (CHIME) Act, which was set to expire the following month. The senators warned that if the funding for the Community Health Center Fund (CHCF) was allowed to expire, it "would cause an estimated 2,400 site closures, 47,000 lost jobs, and threaten the health care of approximately 9 million Americans."[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-53)

### Fiscal policy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Fiscal policy")]

On October 11, 2011, Shaheen voted to proceed with a proposed bill that included $446 billion in spending on infrastructure and schools and provided funding for state and local governments, as well as an extension of the payroll tax deduction. The spending would have been paid for by a 5.6% surtax on incomes above $1 million. The bill failed to obtain cloture.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-54)

Shaheen used an earmark in a large appropriations bill to restore funding for a federal prison in Berlin, NH, despite a $276 million recommended cut.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-56)

### Gun policy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Gun policy")]

Shaheen supports making it illegal for individuals on the terrorist watchlist to buy guns[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-Brindley1005g-57) and voted in favor of a bill proposing to expand background checks for gun purchases.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-58) She also voted to ban magazines of over 10 bullets.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-59) In 2016, she participated in the [Chris Murphy gun control filibuster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_gun_control_filibuster "Chris Murphy gun control filibuster") in the wake of the [Orlando nightclub shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_nightclub_shooting "Orlando nightclub shooting"). Shaheen said that "moments of sympathy are not enough" and that common-sense gun laws must be enacted.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-Mallon1005g-60)

### Energy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Energy")]

Following the [BP oil spill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepwater_Horizon_oil_spill "Deepwater Horizon oil spill") in the Gulf of Mexico in 2010, Shaheen proposed abolishing the [Minerals Management Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minerals_Management_Service "Minerals Management Service"), the U.S. government agency tasked with regulating offshore drilling, arguing that reform had been insufficient and that a new agency was needed.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-61) Shaheen also proposed legislation giving the president's bipartisan [BP Oil Spill Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Commission_on_the_BP_Deepwater_Horizon_Oil_Spill_and_Offshore_Drilling "National Commission on the BP Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill and Offshore Drilling") subpoena power in its investigation.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-62) She argued that subpoena power was necessary to avoid another such disaster, emphasizing the spill's economic costs to the Gulf Coast region and the economy as a whole.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-63)

On April 28, 2014, Shaheen introduced the [Energy Savings and Industrial Competitiveness Act of 2014 (S. 2262; 113th Congress)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_Savings_and_Industrial_Competitiveness_Act_of_2014_(S._2262;_113th_Congress) "Energy Savings and Industrial Competitiveness Act of 2014 (S. 2262; 113th Congress)"), a bill intended to improve [efficient energy use](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efficient_energy_use "Efficient energy use").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-NYTdavenport-64)

In March 2019 Shaheen was an original cosponsor of a bipartisan bill intended to mandate that the Environmental Protection Agency declare per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances as hazardous substances that can be addressed with cleanup funds via the EPA Superfund law and require that polluters undertake or pay for remediation within a year of the bill's enaction.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-65)

Shaheen opposed [Nord Stream 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nord_Stream_2 "Nord Stream 2"), a pipeline for delivering [natural gas from Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_in_the_European_energy_sector "Russia in the European energy sector") to Germany.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-66)

### Iraq War

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Iraq War")]

In 2002, when Shaheen narrowly lost to Sununu, she supported both the [2003 invasion of Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_invasion_of_Iraq "2003 invasion of Iraq") and "regime change" for Iraq.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-supported_war-67) Shaheen said that she came to supporting the policy of removing Saddam Hussein from power after meeting with former Clinton-administration National Security Advisor [Sandy Berger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandy_Berger "Sandy Berger"). According to the _Concord Monitor_ and Associated Press, the issue was a minor one in the race.

Shaheen later questioned [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush")'s handling of the situation in Iraq. In a September 2004 televised interview as Kerry presidential campaign chair she said:[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-68)

> George [W.] Bush has taken us in the wrong direction. He misled us into war in Iraq. That war has not made us safer and more secure at home ... You know, we have not stabilized Afghanistan. We have not stabilized Iraq. There is no plan to win the peace.

On July 28, 2004, while serving as Chair of the Kerry-Edwards Campaign, Shaheen answered questions about her prior support of the Iraq war during an interview on C-SPAN.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-69)

> George [W.] Bush said that the reason we needed to go to war in Iraq, the reason we needed to remove Saddam Hussein, was because he had weapons of mass destruction, weapons that could be used against this country, because he had ties to al-Qaeda and the terrorists who were responsible for the September 11 tragedy. What we know now and what George Bush and Dick Cheney have admitted is that in fact Saddam Hussein did not have weapons of mass destruction. (...) The links to al-Qaeda that the president talked about were not there. (...) While I appreciate that there was an effort to make people in this country think that [there was a connection] (...) the fact is that's not true.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-70)

### LGBT rights

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: LGBT rights")]

Shaheen initially opposed [same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage "Same-sex marriage") as Governor of New Hampshire, but in 2009 she came out in favor of [marriage for same-sex couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_New_Hampshire "Same-sex marriage in New Hampshire") and sponsored the [Respect for Marriage Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respect_for_Marriage_Act "Respect for Marriage Act").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-72) She also voted in favor of the [repeal of](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Ask,_Don't_Tell_Repeal_Act_of_2010 "Don't Ask, Don't Tell Repeal Act of 2010")[Don't ask, don't tell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_ask,_don't_tell "Don't ask, don't tell"), and supports government recognition of same-sex spouses of military and other government personnel.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-73)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

### Minimum wage

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Minimum wage")]

On March 5, 2021, Shaheen voted against [Bernie Sanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Sanders "Bernie Sanders")'s amendment to include a $15/hour [minimum wage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_wage_in_the_United_States "Minimum wage in the United States") in the [American Rescue Plan Act of 2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Rescue_Plan_Act_of_2021 "American Rescue Plan Act of 2021").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-74)

### Immigration

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Immigration")]

In 2025, Shaheen was one of 12 Senate Democrats who joined all Republicans to vote for the [Laken Riley Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laken_Riley_Act "Laken Riley Act").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-75)

### Sudanese civil war

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Sudanese civil war")]

Main article: [Sudanese civil war (2023–present)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudanese_civil_war_(2023%E2%80%93present) "Sudanese civil war (2023–present)")

In October 2025, after the [Rapid Support Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_Support_Forces "Rapid Support Forces") (RSF) [captured El Fasher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_El_Fasher "Siege of El Fasher") in [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan"), Shaheen denounced the RSF [massacre of local civilians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Fasher_massacre "El Fasher massacre"), urged that the RSF be designated a terrorist organization, and harshly criticized the [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates") for its support of the RSF.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-76)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Shaheen is married to William Shaheen, an attorney and judge. They have three children together. Their daughter Stefany Shaheen is a candidate for [New Hampshire's 1st congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire's_1st_congressional_district "New Hampshire's 1st congressional district") in [2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_New_Hampshire "2026 United States House of Representatives elections in New Hampshire").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-77) She publicly opposed her mother's position on the [2025 federal government shutdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_United_States_federal_government_shutdown "2025 United States federal government shutdown").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-78)

Jeanne and William Shaheen formerly owned a store in New Hampshire that sold used jewelry.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-79) In June 2025, the [Department of Homeland Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Homeland_Security "United States Department of Homeland Security") (DHS) published a press release alleging that Senator Shaheen intervened to remove her husband from enhanced [Transportation Security Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transportation_Security_Administration "Transportation Security Administration") (TSA) scrutiny. After she contacted TSA, he was reportedly removed from the list and exempted from enhanced screening. DHS characterized this as evidence of politicization in the Biden administration's watchlisting process and accused the program of being used to benefit political allies.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-80)

**Cynthia Jeanne Shaheen** ([/ˈ dʒ iː n ʃ ə ˈ h iː n/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_JEEN shə-HEEN_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); née **Bowers**, born January 28, 1947) is an American politician and former educator serving since 2009 as the [senior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seniority_in_the_United_States_Senate "Seniority in the United States Senate")[United States senator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") from [New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire "New Hampshire"). A member of the [Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)"), she served from 1997 to 2003 as the [78th governor of New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_Hampshire "List of governors of New Hampshire"). Shaheen is the first woman elected both [governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_(United_States) "Governor (United States)") and a U.S. senator, and was the first elected [female governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States "List of female governors in the United States") of New Hampshire.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-1)

After serving two terms in the [New Hampshire Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire_Senate "New Hampshire Senate"), Shaheen was elected governor in [1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_New_Hampshire_gubernatorial_election "1996 New Hampshire gubernatorial election") and reelected in [1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_New_Hampshire_gubernatorial_election "1998 New Hampshire gubernatorial election") and [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_New_Hampshire_gubernatorial_election "2000 New Hampshire gubernatorial election"). In [2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "2002 United States Senate election in New Hampshire"), she unsuccessfully ran for the U.S. Senate against [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") nominee [John E. Sununu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_E._Sununu "John E. Sununu"). She served as director of the [Harvard Institute of Politics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Institute_of_Politics "Harvard Institute of Politics") before resigning to run for the U.S. Senate again in the [2008 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "2008 United States Senate election in New Hampshire"), defeating Sununu in a rematch. She has been the dean of [New Hampshire’s congressional delegation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire's_congressional_delegations "New Hampshire's congressional delegations") since 2011, when Senator [Judd Gregg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judd_Gregg "Judd Gregg") retired.

Shaheen became the first Democratic senator from New Hampshire since [John A. Durkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_A._Durkin "John A. Durkin"). In [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "2014 United States Senate election in New Hampshire"), she became the second Democrat from New Hampshire to be reelected to the Senate since [Thomas J. McIntyre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_J._McIntyre "Thomas J. McIntyre") in [1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "1972 United States Senate election in New Hampshire"). She was reelected to a third term in [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "2020 United States Senate election in New Hampshire"). Upon [Dianne Feinstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dianne_Feinstein "Dianne Feinstein")'s death in 2023, Shaheen became the oldest serving female U.S. senator. On March 12, 2025, she announced that she would not seek reelection in [2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "2026 United States Senate election in New Hampshire").

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Jeanne Shaheen was born Cynthia Jeanne Bowers in [St. Charles, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri "St. Charles, Missouri"), the daughter of Belle Ernestine (Stillings) and Ivan E. Bowers.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-2)[_[unreliable source?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable\_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")_]

Shaheen graduated from high school in [Selinsgrove, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selinsgrove,_Pennsylvania "Selinsgrove, Pennsylvania"), and earned a bachelor's degree in English from [Shippensburg University of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shippensburg_University_of_Pennsylvania "Shippensburg University of Pennsylvania") and a master's degree in political science from the [University of Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Mississippi "University of Mississippi").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-10things-3) She taught high school in [Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi "Mississippi")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-4) and moved to New Hampshire in 1973, where she also taught school.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-5)

## Early political career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early political career")]

As a [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Democratic_Party "United States Democratic Party"), she worked on several campaigns, including [Jimmy Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter "Jimmy Carter")'s 1976 presidential campaign, and as the New Hampshire campaign manager for [Gary Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Hart "Gary Hart") in 1984,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-6) before running for office in 1990, when she was elected to the [state Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire_Senate "New Hampshire Senate") for the [21st district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire's_21st_State_Senate_District "New Hampshire's 21st State Senate District"). She was elected [governor of New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_New_Hampshire "Governor of New Hampshire") in 1996 and reelected in 1998 and 2000.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-7)

In April 2005, Shaheen was named director of Harvard's Institute of Politics,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-8) succeeding former U.S. Representative and Secretary of Agriculture [Dan Glickman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Glickman "Dan Glickman").

## Governorship

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Governorship")]

Shaheen's decision to run for New Hampshire governor followed the retirement of Republican Governor [Steve Merrill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Merrill "Steve Merrill"). Her opponent in 1996 was [Ovide M. Lamontagne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovide_M._Lamontagne "Ovide M. Lamontagne"), then chairman of the State Board of Education. Shaheen presented herself as a moderate. According to a PBS profile, she focused on education funding issues, and pledged to expand kindergarten. She defeated Lamontagne by 87,854 votes.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-9)

Shaheen was the first woman to be elected governor of New Hampshire.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-10) (She was not, however, the first woman to serve as New Hampshire's governor; [Vesta M. Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vesta_M._Roy "Vesta M. Roy") was acting governor from December 30, 1982, until January 6, 1983.)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-11)

In 1998, she was reelected by 112,296 votes.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-13)

In both 1996 and 1998, Shaheen took a no-new-taxes pledge. After a court decision preventing education from being largely supported by local taxes, "her administration devised a plan that would have increased education spending and set a statewide property tax."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-14)

Running for a third term in 2000, Shaheen refused to renew her no-new-taxes pledge, becoming the first New Hampshire governor in 38 years to win an election without making that pledge.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-15) Shaheen's preferred solution to the school-funding problem was not a broad-based tax but legalized video-gambling at state racetracks—a solution repeatedly rejected by the state legislature.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-17)

In 2001, Shaheen tried to implement a 2.5% sales tax, the first broad-based tariff of its kind in New Hampshire, which has never had a sales tax. The state legislature rejected her proposal.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-18) She also proposed an increase in the state's cigarette tax and a 4.5% capital gains tax.

## Presidential politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Presidential politics")]

### 2000

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2000")]

During the [2000 Democratic presidential primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States)_presidential_primaries,_2000 "Democratic Party (United States) presidential primaries, 2000") in New Hampshire, Shaheen supported [Al Gore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore "Al Gore"), and her husband served as Gore's New Hampshire campaign manager. According to the _New York Observer_, the Shaheens were critical in helping Gore win a narrow victory in the New Hampshire primary over [Bill Bradley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Bradley "Bill Bradley").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-20)

Gore added Shaheen to his short list of potential vice presidential nominees, which also included Indiana Senator [Evan Bayh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Bayh "Evan Bayh"), North Carolina Senator [John Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Edwards "John Edwards"), House Minority Leader [Dick Gephardt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Gephardt "Dick Gephardt"), Massachusetts Senator [John Kerry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry "John Kerry"), and Connecticut Senator [Joe Lieberman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Lieberman "Joe Lieberman").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-21) Shaheen responded to speculation by stating she wasn't interested in the job.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-22) There has since been discussion over whether Gore would have won the election had he picked Shaheen as his running mate.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-24)

### 2004

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2004")]

After a short time teaching at [Harvard University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University") (and a fellowship in the Institute of Politics with former Massachusetts Governor [Jane Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane_Swift "Jane Swift")), Shaheen was named national chairperson of [John Kerry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry "John Kerry")'s [2004 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry_presidential_campaign,_2004 "John Kerry presidential campaign, 2004") in September 2003.

## U.S. Senate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: U.S. Senate")]

#### 2002

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2002")]

Main article: [2002 United States Senate election in New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "2002 United States Senate election in New Hampshire")

After three two-year terms as governor, Shaheen declined to run for a fourth, instead choosing to run for the U.S. Senate in [2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Senate_election,_2002 "U.S. Senate election, 2002"). Republican [John E. Sununu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_E._Sununu "John E. Sununu") defeated her by 19,751 votes. In an interview with the _[Concord Monitor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concord\_Monitor "Concord Monitor")_, Shaheen attributed her loss in part to "discussion about the job that [she] did as governor." At that time, early Republican advertisements slammed her support for putting a sales tax on the ballot or faulted her for failing schools.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-25)

In June 2004, former Republican consultant [Allen Raymond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Raymond "Allen Raymond") pleaded guilty to [jamming the phone lines of the New Hampshire Democratic Party's 2002 get-out-the-vote operation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_New_Hampshire_Senate_election_phone_jamming_scandal "2002 New Hampshire Senate election phone jamming scandal"); some believe this interference contributed to Shaheen's loss, including former Senator [Bob Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_C._Smith "Robert C. Smith"), whom Sununu had defeated in the Republican primary.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-26) In February 2005, a judge sentenced Raymond to five months in prison. Former state GOP executive director [Charles McGee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_McGee_(politician) "Charles McGee (politician)") was sentenced to seven months for his role.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-28)

Raymond alleged that [James Tobin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Tobin_(political_operative) "James Tobin (political operative)"), [Northeast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northeastern_United_States "Northeastern United States") field director for the [National Republican Senatorial Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Republican_Senatorial_Committee "National Republican Senatorial Committee"), masterminded the plot. In December 2005, Tobin was convicted of two federal felonies arising from the phone-jamming and sentenced to ten months in prison, but his conviction was reversed on appeal. In October 2008, prosecutors filed two new felony indictments charging that Tobin lied to an FBI agent when he was interviewed in 2003 about his role in the phone-jamming case.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-29) These charges were summarily dismissed in 2009 after the federal judge in Maine's District Court found them motivated by "vindictive prosecution".[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-Harrison-30)

#### 2008

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2008")]

Main article: [2008 United States Senate election in New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "2008 United States Senate election in New Hampshire")

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/Jeanne_Shaheen%2C_official_Senate_photo_portrait%2C_2009.jpg/250px-Jeanne_Shaheen%2C_official_Senate_photo_portrait%2C_2009.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jeanne_Shaheen,_official_Senate_photo_portrait,_2009.jpg)

Official portrait, 2009

In early July 2007, University of New Hampshire Survey Center poll found that even though Shaheen had not yet announced whether she would run for Senate, she would beat Sununu in the 2008 Senate race 54–38. By contrast, all the Democratic candidates already in the race trailed Sununu in polling.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-31)

In April 2007, Shaheen met with Senate Majority Leader [Harry Reid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Reid "Harry Reid") and [Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Senatorial_Campaign_Committee "Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee") Chairman [Chuck Schumer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Schumer "Chuck Schumer") about a Senate run. Both said she would have strong support from the DSCC if she ran. On September 14, 2007, Shaheen announced her candidacy.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-32) On September 15, she formally launched her campaign at her home in [Madbury, New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madbury,_New_Hampshire "Madbury, New Hampshire"). On September 21, [EMILY's List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMILY's_List "EMILY's List") endorsed her campaign.

Shaheen defeated Sununu by 44,535 votes.

On election night, even as her party lost control of the Senate, Shaheen won reelection by 15,837 votes. As a measure of how Republican New Hampshire once was, Shaheen is only the second Democrat in the state's history to win two terms in the Senate.

#### 2020

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2020")]

Main article: [2020 United States Senate election in New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_Hampshire "2020 United States Senate election in New Hampshire")

Shaheen was reelected in 2020 defeating Republican nominee Bryant "Corky" Messner by 124,549 votes. She is the first New Hampshire Democrat elected to three full terms in the Senate. The only other Democrat to be popularly elected more than once from New Hampshire, [Thomas J. McIntyre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_J._McIntyre "Thomas J. McIntyre") (who held the seat Shaheen currently holds), served the remainder of [Styles Bridges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Styles_Bridges "Styles Bridges")'s last term before being elected to two terms in his own right.

On January 3, 2009, Shaheen was sworn in to the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate"). As a senator, she has sponsored 288 bills, five of which have become law.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-37)

On January 6, 2021, Shaheen was participating in the certification of the [2021 United States Electoral College vote count](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_United_States_Electoral_College_vote_count "2021 United States Electoral College vote count") when Trump supporters [attacked the U.S. Capitol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_6_United_States_Capitol_attack "January 6 United States Capitol attack"). She tweeted during the attack that she and her staff were safe and that "We will not be stopped from doing our Constitutional duty".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-West-38) The day after the attack, Shaheen called Trump "unfit for office" and said that she supported impeaching him and removing him from office.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-Brewer-39)

In 2024, Shaheen was ranked among the top 10 most bipartisan senators.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-40)

## Political positions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Political positions")]

### Healthcare

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Healthcare")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Healthcare_Presser_Gallery_073119_%2899_of_117%29_%2848424636752%29.jpg/250px-Healthcare_Presser_Gallery_073119_%2899_of_117%29_%2848424636752%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Healthcare_Presser_Gallery_073119_(99_of_117)_(48424636752).jpg)

Shaheen speaks on health care, 2019

In 2009, Shaheen partnered with U.S. Senator [Susan Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Collins_(politician) "Susan Collins (politician)") to introduce the Medicare Transitional Care Act, which provides follow-up care for discharged hospital patients to reduce re-hospitalizations.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-45) The bill passed in 2010,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-46) and research at the [University of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania "University of Pennsylvania") predicted the measure would lower the cost of healthcare by as much as $5,000 per Medicare beneficiary while also improving healthcare quality and reducing re-hospitalizations.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-47)

In December 2009, Shaheen voted for the [Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affordable_Care_Act "Affordable Care Act") (Obamacare).[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-49)

Before the rollout of the ACA, Shaheen said that people who liked their current healthcare plans could keep them.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-50) When asked about people who were losing their healthcare plans due to the ACA, Shaheen said they could keep their plans if they were "willing to pay more".[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-51)

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/U.S._Senator_Jeanne_Shaheen%2C_U.S._Congressman_Joe_Wilson%2C_U.S._envoy_to_Syria_Tom_Barrack%2C_and_Syrian_President_Ahmed_al-Sharaa_%282025%29.jpg/250px-U.S._Senator_Jeanne_Shaheen%2C_U.S._Congressman_Joe_Wilson%2C_U.S._envoy_to_Syria_Tom_Barrack%2C_and_Syrian_President_Ahmed_al-Sharaa_%282025%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:U.S._Senator_Jeanne_Shaheen,_U.S._Congressman_Joe_Wilson,_U.S._envoy_to_Syria_Tom_Barrack,_and_Syrian_President_Ahmed_al-Sharaa_(2025).jpg)

Shaheen, U.S. Congressman [Joe Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Wilson "Joe Wilson"), and U.S. envoy to Syria [Tom Barrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Barrack "Tom Barrack") met with Syrian President [Ahmed al-Sharaa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_al-Sharaa "Ahmed al-Sharaa"), August 2025

In August 2019, Shaheen was one of 19 senators to sign a letter to [Treasury Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_the_Treasury "United States Secretary of the Treasury")[Steven Mnuchin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Mnuchin "Steven Mnuchin") and [Health and Human Services Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Health_and_Human_Services "United States Secretary of Health and Human Services")[Alex Azar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Azar "Alex Azar") requesting data from the Trump administration to help states and Congress understand the potential consequences of the _Texas v. United States Affordable Care Act_ lawsuit, writing that an overhaul of the present health care system would form "an enormous hole in the pocketbooks of the people we serve as well as wreck state budgets".[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-52)

In October 2019, Shaheen was one of 27 senators to sign a letter to Senate Majority Leader [Mitch McConnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitch_McConnell "Mitch McConnell") and Senate Minority Leader [Chuck Schumer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Schumer "Chuck Schumer") advocating the passage of the Community Health Investment, Modernization, and Excellence (CHIME) Act, which was set to expire the following month. The senators warned that if the funding for the Community Health Center Fund (CHCF) was allowed to expire, it "would cause an estimated 2,400 site closures, 47,000 lost jobs, and threaten the health care of approximately 9 million Americans."[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-53)

### Fiscal policy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Fiscal policy")]

On October 11, 2011, Shaheen voted to proceed with a proposed bill that included $446 billion in spending on infrastructure and schools and provided funding for state and local governments, as well as an extension of the payroll tax deduction. The spending would have been paid for by a 5.6% surtax on incomes above $1 million. The bill failed to obtain cloture.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-54)

Shaheen used an earmark in a large appropriations bill to restore funding for a federal prison in Berlin, NH, despite a $276 million recommended cut.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-56)

### Gun policy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Gun policy")]

Shaheen supports making it illegal for individuals on the terrorist watchlist to buy guns[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-Brindley1005g-57) and voted in favor of a bill proposing to expand background checks for gun purchases.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-58) She also voted to ban magazines of over 10 bullets.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-59) In 2016, she participated in the [Chris Murphy gun control filibuster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy_gun_control_filibuster "Chris Murphy gun control filibuster") in the wake of the [Orlando nightclub shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_nightclub_shooting "Orlando nightclub shooting"). Shaheen said that "moments of sympathy are not enough" and that common-sense gun laws must be enacted.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-Mallon1005g-60)

### Energy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Energy")]

Following the [BP oil spill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepwater_Horizon_oil_spill "Deepwater Horizon oil spill") in the Gulf of Mexico in 2010, Shaheen proposed abolishing the [Minerals Management Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minerals_Management_Service "Minerals Management Service"), the U.S. government agency tasked with regulating offshore drilling, arguing that reform had been insufficient and that a new agency was needed.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-61) Shaheen also proposed legislation giving the president's bipartisan [BP Oil Spill Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Commission_on_the_BP_Deepwater_Horizon_Oil_Spill_and_Offshore_Drilling "National Commission on the BP Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill and Offshore Drilling") subpoena power in its investigation.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-62) She argued that subpoena power was necessary to avoid another such disaster, emphasizing the spill's economic costs to the Gulf Coast region and the economy as a whole.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-63)

On April 28, 2014, Shaheen introduced the [Energy Savings and Industrial Competitiveness Act of 2014 (S. 2262; 113th Congress)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_Savings_and_Industrial_Competitiveness_Act_of_2014_(S._2262;_113th_Congress) "Energy Savings and Industrial Competitiveness Act of 2014 (S. 2262; 113th Congress)"), a bill intended to improve [efficient energy use](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efficient_energy_use "Efficient energy use").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-NYTdavenport-64)

In March 2019 Shaheen was an original cosponsor of a bipartisan bill intended to mandate that the Environmental Protection Agency declare per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances as hazardous substances that can be addressed with cleanup funds via the EPA Superfund law and require that polluters undertake or pay for remediation within a year of the bill's enaction.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-65)

Shaheen opposed [Nord Stream 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nord_Stream_2 "Nord Stream 2"), a pipeline for delivering [natural gas from Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_in_the_European_energy_sector "Russia in the European energy sector") to Germany.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-66)

### Iraq War

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Iraq War")]

In 2002, when Shaheen narrowly lost to Sununu, she supported both the [2003 invasion of Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_invasion_of_Iraq "2003 invasion of Iraq") and "regime change" for Iraq.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-supported_war-67) Shaheen said that she came to supporting the policy of removing Saddam Hussein from power after meeting with former Clinton-administration National Security Advisor [Sandy Berger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandy_Berger "Sandy Berger"). According to the _Concord Monitor_ and Associated Press, the issue was a minor one in the race.

Shaheen later questioned [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush")'s handling of the situation in Iraq. In a September 2004 televised interview as Kerry presidential campaign chair she said:[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-68)

> George [W.] Bush has taken us in the wrong direction. He misled us into war in Iraq. That war has not made us safer and more secure at home ... You know, we have not stabilized Afghanistan. We have not stabilized Iraq. There is no plan to win the peace.

On July 28, 2004, while serving as Chair of the Kerry-Edwards Campaign, Shaheen answered questions about her prior support of the Iraq war during an interview on C-SPAN.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-69)

> George [W.] Bush said that the reason we needed to go to war in Iraq, the reason we needed to remove Saddam Hussein, was because he had weapons of mass destruction, weapons that could be used against this country, because he had ties to al-Qaeda and the terrorists who were responsible for the September 11 tragedy. What we know now and what George Bush and Dick Cheney have admitted is that in fact Saddam Hussein did not have weapons of mass destruction. (...) The links to al-Qaeda that the president talked about were not there. (...) While I appreciate that there was an effort to make people in this country think that [there was a connection] (...) the fact is that's not true.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-70)

### War in Afghanistan

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: War in Afghanistan")]

Shaheen opposed the [2021 withdrawal of U.S. troops from Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Withdrawal_of_United_States_troops_from_Afghanistan_(2020%E2%80%932021) "Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan (2020–2021)") under President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-71)

### LGBT rights

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: LGBT rights")]

Shaheen initially opposed [same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage "Same-sex marriage") as Governor of New Hampshire, but in 2009 she came out in favor of [marriage for same-sex couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_New_Hampshire "Same-sex marriage in New Hampshire") and sponsored the [Respect for Marriage Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respect_for_Marriage_Act "Respect for Marriage Act").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-72) She also voted in favor of the [repeal of](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Ask,_Don't_Tell_Repeal_Act_of_2010 "Don't Ask, Don't Tell Repeal Act of 2010")[Don't ask, don't tell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_ask,_don't_tell "Don't ask, don't tell"), and supports government recognition of same-sex spouses of military and other government personnel.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-73)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

### Minimum wage

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Minimum wage")]

On March 5, 2021, Shaheen voted against [Bernie Sanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Sanders "Bernie Sanders")'s amendment to include a $15/hour [minimum wage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_wage_in_the_United_States "Minimum wage in the United States") in the [American Rescue Plan Act of 2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Rescue_Plan_Act_of_2021 "American Rescue Plan Act of 2021").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-74)

### Immigration

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Immigration")]

In 2025, Shaheen was one of 12 Senate Democrats who joined all Republicans to vote for the [Laken Riley Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laken_Riley_Act "Laken Riley Act").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-75)

### Sudanese civil war

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Sudanese civil war")]

Main article: [Sudanese civil war (2023–present)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudanese_civil_war_(2023%E2%80%93present) "Sudanese civil war (2023–present)")

In October 2025, after the [Rapid Support Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_Support_Forces "Rapid Support Forces") (RSF) [captured El Fasher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_El_Fasher "Siege of El Fasher") in [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan"), Shaheen denounced the RSF [massacre of local civilians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Fasher_massacre "El Fasher massacre"), urged that the RSF be designated a terrorist organization, and harshly criticized the [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates") for its support of the RSF.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-76)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jeanne_Shaheen&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Shaheen is married to William Shaheen, an attorney and judge. They have three children together. Their daughter Stefany Shaheen is a candidate for [New Hampshire's 1st congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire's_1st_congressional_district "New Hampshire's 1st congressional district") in [2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_New_Hampshire "2026 United States House of Representatives elections in New Hampshire").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-77) She publicly opposed her mother's position on the [2025 federal government shutdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_United_States_federal_government_shutdown "2025 United States federal government shutdown").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-78)

Jeanne and William Shaheen formerly owned a store in New Hampshire that sold used jewelry.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-79) In June 2025, the [Department of Homeland Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Homeland_Security "United States Department of Homeland Security") (DHS) published a press release alleging that Senator Shaheen intervened to remove her husband from enhanced [Transportation Security Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transportation_Security_Administration "Transportation Security Administration") (TSA) scrutiny. After she contacted TSA, he was reportedly removed from the list and exempted from enhanced screening. DHS characterized this as evidence of politicization in the Biden administration's watchlisting process and accused the program of being used to benefit political allies.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Shaheen#cite_note-80)
